Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — clarifying GPU mix & TPS targets

Thanks again for the call earlier, Alex / Jamie — good discussion. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we’re aligned: 

- High-level ask: you’re leaning toward Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) because the application needs predictable token-level unit economics and steady low-latency inference at scale.
- Items we still need to size accurately: steady-state TPS target, burst TPS, expected average prompt/response token counts, 95th/99th p99 latency SLOs, and any model/quantization constraints.
- Attached: capacity_workbook.xlsx — please fill the orange fields (TPS by endpoint, sample token distributions, peak windows) and return. We’ll use that to run a bench and propose two sizing options (cost-first & latency-first).

Next steps:
1) You fill and return capacity_workbook.xlsx by EOD Mon (2026-09-06).
2) We’ll line up a short profiling POC (1–2 days) once we have sample traffic; goal is to validate GPU family tradeoffs (A100 vs H100) and batching thresholds.
3) Follow-up call to review sizing options and estimated monthly committed spend.

Two quick clarifications from today’s notes:
- Security: you mentioned VPC + KMS requirement for some telemetry — we can run Dedicated inside a VPC/private subnet and integrate with your KMS.
- Tokenization variance: if your prompts include lots of long context (code, logs), that will increase token cost; please flag heavy tokenizers.

Thanks — feel free to reply inline.

Thanks Diego — quick answers inline and a few asks: 

- Steady-state TPS: ~1,200 inference calls/sec across two endpoints (semantic search + chat).
- Burst TPS: peaks to ~2,500 TPS during morning batch window (9–10am PDT), expect ~10 minute peaks.
- Token mix: average prompt ~80 tokens, average response ~120 tokens, but ~15% of requests include long context (~800 tokens) for retrieval-augmented generation.
- Concurrency: about 90–120 concurrent sessions during peaks (many short-lived).
- Compliance: we need private networking for logs and encrypted at rest; prefer to keep telemetry off if possible.

Question: on GPU family — we’re evaluating H100 vs A100-80GB. Our infra lead wants to understand the expected latency delta and rough cost delta for dedicated pools. Also curious if Redwood supports mixed pools (some H100 + some A100) and automatic routing.

We’ll fill the workbook and return by Monday. Also attaching a small sample query set (will send separately).

—Alex

Appreciate the quick answers, Alex — that token distribution helps a lot. High-level guidance and two candidate sizing options below; these are intentionally coarse until we run a short benchmark with your sample traffic.

Short answers: yes, Redwood supports mixed pools and smart routing by policy (latency-priority vs cost-priority). For your profile (1.2k steady / 2.5k peak, 15% long-context):

Option A — Latency-first (recommended if p99 < 300ms matters)
- GPU family: H100 (NVL-accelerated kernels)
- Pool size: 3–4 H100s (start 3, burst to 4)
- Expected steady throughput (GPT-like model, FP16): ~1,000–1,400 TPS depending on batching; long-context requests will reduce effective throughput for those sessions.
- Notes: Lower p99, better single-request latency, higher cost.

Option B — Cost-first (mixed pool)
- GPU family: A100 80GB + int8/4-bit quantization for most traffic, H100 for long-context/cold-call routing
- Pool mix: 5x A100 + 1x H100 as a hot-path for heavy-context/infrequent large jobs
- Expected steady throughput: A100 pool handles ~1,500 TPS for short/medium contexts; H100 absorbs long-context spikes and p99-sensitive queries.
- Notes: More cost-efficient, requires model quantization testing and a small routing layer.

POC proposal:
- Benchmark window: 48 hours using your sample traffic and the workbook numbers.
- Goals: validate throughput per GPU, p50/p95/p99 latency curves, memory/kv-cache behavior for retrieval flows.

Attachments: I filled a copy of your workbook with our estimated per-endpoint TPS columns (capacity_workbook_filled.xlsx).

Let me know if you want a quick 30-minute call Monday to walk through the two options and pick POC targets. I’ll loop Karthik for kernel/quant notes and Monica for ops/runbook items.

--

Adding a couple of technical notes from the infra side: 

- Concurrency semantics: the combination of many short sessions + long-context RAG queries will create tail variance. We suggest we capture 2–3 hours of peak traces (sampled) to characterize KV cache hit rates and token distribution. That will materially affect A100 vs H100 sizing.
- Quantization risk: if you want to run int8/4-bit quantized weights on A100, we need to validate quality on your eval set — we can include this as a small step in the POC.
- Mixed pools: routing is straightforward; we expose policy flags per route (latency_preferred, cost_preferred, long_context_hotpath).

Action items before we book the POC:
1) Flowlytics shares a 2–3 hour sample trace from a peak window (anonymized) and the filled workbook.
2) Redwood creates two bench configurations and shares an expected delta (cost/month + expected p95/p99) within 48 hours of receiving the trace.

I’m available Tue afternoon for a short call to finalize POC targets.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
